Meet the Japanese stoat, a carnivorous creature living in the subalpine areas of central and northern Honshu. These high-altitude animals are members of the weasel family and can be found at elevations of over 1,200 meters. ✨ These wildly cute critters have incredible coats, which go from chestnut brown with a white underbelly in summer to nearly totally white in winter — only the tips of their tails have color, a bold black. ❄️ But don't be fooled by their cuddly exterior — Japanese stoats are feisty, with a fierce temperament and enough power to take down larger birds and wild rabbits when hungry. 🐇😮Most of the time, however, they stick to hunting field mice and insects. 🐁 🐛🪲 When exploring Oze's subalpine zones, keep your ears open for a high-pitched "kii!" coming from the bushes. If you're lucky enough to spot a stoat, you can get a "stoat discovery card" at the Oze Yamanoh
